mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the monthly FEDFUNDS rate above 1.5% for three consecutive months predicts a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to anticipated tightening of credit conditions.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 1.5% and remains above for 3 consecutive months
regime_hint: early stage of a tightening cycle
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero in the tightening regime (p > 0.05), or FEDFUNDS reverts below 1.5% within 2 months.

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly UNRATE falls below 3.5% for two consecutive months, labor market slack increases, reducing expected corporate profit margins and driving a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in >50% of similar labor-loosening periods (empirical frequency), or UNRATE recovers above 3.5% within 4 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly increase in HOUST (household spending index) above its 12-month prior value by at least 5% predicts a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return as it signals accelerated consumer demand.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically significant (p > 0.05) or HOUST growth is not sustained for 2 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly INDPRO (industrial production) index exceeds its 12-month moving average by at least 8%, it indicates supply-side expansion that precedes a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain negative in >70% of such supply-expansion events (backtest frequency).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly declines in CPIAUCSL of at least 0.3% for three months indicate accelerating inflation expectations, which drive a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL decreases by >0.3% each month for 3 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during such inflationary signals.

mechanism_narrative: A two-standard-deviation drop in PAYEMS (employment months) within a single month predicts a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return as it reflects labor market stress and reduced consumer spending.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not negative in >80% of such labor-stress events (walk-forward).

mechanism_narrative: When the combination of GDPC1 (GDP) and HOUST shows a cross above their 50-day moving average simultaneously, it indicates a dual demand impulse that drives a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) in 70% of such dual-signal events.

mechanism_narrative: During a regime where UNRATE > 4% and INDPRO is above its 12-month moving average, supply constraints are easing, which predicts a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: regime: UNRATE > 4% AND INDPRO > INDPRO[12m moving average]
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not positive in >60% of such regime windows (walk-forward).
